original_title: Owlcat co-founder says the studio won't turn its back on hardcore RPGs as it hits 600 employees and preps its own Mass Effect killer
summary_en: The acclaimed RPG developer Owlcat Games, now boasting 600 employees, has reaffirmed its commitment to deep, complex CRPGs. This comes as the studio prepares to launch ambitious new titles that push the boundaries of its established formula.

en.title: Owlcat Games Confirms Hardcore RPG Focus Amidst Massive Studio Growth
en.summary: The acclaimed RPG developer Owlcat Games, now boasting 600 employees, has reaffirmed its commitment to deep, complex CRPGs. This comes as the studio prepares to launch ambitious new titles that push the boundaries of its established formula.
en.body:
Owlcat Games, the studio behind beloved CRPGs like **Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous** and **Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader**, has reached a significant milestone, expanding its team to a formidable 600 employees. This growth coincides with the studio's 10th anniversary and a clear declaration from co-founder and creative director **Alexander Mishulin** that the company remains steadfastly committed to its hardcore RPG roots.

"We will continue to make CRPGs because we love them," Mishulin stated in a recent interview. "We do not want to become stagnant. We will be trying different approaches for our RPG games, trying to find the best possible fit for the idea of the game." This assurance is particularly welcome as Owlcat gears up for its most ambitious projects yet. While the studio's first three titles shared a similar engine and a focus on leading state-level organizations, their upcoming projects represent exciting departures. **The Expanse: Osiris Reborn** is described as a Mass Effect-like experience, indicating a move towards a more cinematic, player-character-centric narrative. This evolution, however, is not a repudiation of their established strengths.

## A Bold New Direction for CRPGs

Owlcat's commitment to the CRPG genre is further evidenced by **Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy**. This title builds upon the studio's established CRPG engine and the ruleset of **Rogue Trader**, suggesting a familiar core experience for long-time fans. Yet, it also marks a significant shift by trading the customary ruler fantasy for an intricate detective and investigation metagame within the grim dark universe of Warhammer 40,000. This blend of familiar mechanics with novel gameplay loops demonstrates Owlcat's desire to innovate within the genre they champion.

## What This Means for Players

For the passionate global fanbase that consumes content on mobile and craves deep, engaging role-playing experiences, this news is a resounding affirmation. Owlcat has consistently delivered games that cater to players who appreciate complex systems, meaningful choices, and rich lore. The studio's expansion to handle multiple ambitious projects simultaneously, while still prioritizing the development of hardcore CRPGs, signals a bright future for fans of the genre. It reassures players that the studio that brought them intricate kingdom management and deep tactical combat is not abandoning its core identity but rather evolving it.

## What's Next

With **The Expanse: Osiris Reborn** and **Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy** in active development, Owlcat Games is poised to release its most diverse slate of titles to date. Specific release windows for these highly anticipated games have not yet been announced, but their simultaneous development signifies a studio at the peak of its creative and technical capabilities.

tr.title: Owlcat Games, Klasik RPG Odaklı Çalışmalarına Devam Ediyor
tr.summary: Ünlü RPG geliştiricisi Owlcat Games, 600 çalışanıyla birlikte klasik RPG odaklı çalışmalarına devam ediyor. Stüdyo, yeni ve iddialı projeler üzerinde çalışırken, klasik RPG formülünü geliştirmeye devam ediyor. Owlcat Games'in bu hamlesi, klasik RPG severler için heyecan verici bir gelişme.
tr.body:
Owlcat Games, **Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous** ve **Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader** gibi sevilen CRPG'lerin arkasındaki stüdyo, önemli bir dönemeçte. 600 çalışanıyla birlikte 10. yılını kutlayan stüdyo, kurucu ortak ve yaratıcı yönetmen **Alexander Mishulin**'in açıklamalarına göre klasik RPG kökenlerine bağlılığını sürdürüyor.

> "CRPG'ler yapmaya devam edeceğiz, çünkü onları seviyoruz" diyen Mishulin, "Sürekli aynı şeyi yapmak istemiyoruz. Farklı yaklaşımlar deneyeceğiz ve oyun fikirlerinin en iyi şekilde uygulanmasına çalışacağız."

Bu açıklama, stüdyonun en iddialı projelerine doğru ilerlerken özellikle wichtig. İlk üç oyunlarında benzer bir motor ve devlet düzeyinde organizasyonlara odaklanan stüdyo, yeni projeleriyle birlikte heyecan verici bir değişim yaşanıyor. **The Expanse: Osiris Reborn**, bir **Mass Effect** benzeri deneyim vaat ediyor ve daha çok sinematik, oyuncu karakteri odaklı bir anlatıya doğru bir hareketi işaret ediyor. Ancak bu, stüdyonun klasik güçlerini reddetmesi anlamına gelmiyor.

## Yeni Bir Yöne Doğru
Owlcat Games'in klasik RPG'ye olan bağlılığı, **Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy** ile daha da güçlü bir şekilde ortaya çıkıyor. Bu oyun, stüdyonun klasik CRPG motorunu ve **Rogue Trader**'in kurallarını temel alıyor, ancak geleneksel fantezi yerine **Warhammer 40,000**'in karanlık ve kasvetli evreninde bir dedektif ve soruşturma meta-oyunu sunuyor. Bu, tanıdık mekaniklerle yeni oyun döngülerinin birleşmesi, stüdyonun klasik RPG türünü geliştirmeye devam etme isteğini gösteriyor.

## Oyuncular İçin Ne Anlama Geliyor
Klasik RPG severler için bu haber, stüdyonun klasik RPG'ye bağlılığını sürdürmesi anlamına geliyor. Owlcat Games, kompleks sistemler, anlamlı seçimler ve zengin lore seven oyunculara hitap eden oyunlar sunmayı sürdürüyor. Stüdyonun, birden fazla iddialı projeyi aynı anda geliştirirken klasik RPG odaklı çalışmalara öncelik vermesi, türün geleceği için olumlu bir işaret.

## Sonraki Adımlar
**The Expanse: Osiris Reborn** ve **Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy** gibi oyunların geliştirilmesiyle birlikte Owlcat Games, en çeşitli oyunlarını piyasaya sürmeye hazırlanıyor. Bu oyunların yayın tarihleri henüz açıklanmasa da, aynı anda geliştirilmeleri stüdyonun yaratıcı ve teknik açıdan zirve noktada olduğunu gösteriyor.

content_raw: In a new interview with PCGamesN to mark Owlcat's 10th anniversary, studio co-founder and creative director Alexander Mishulin talked about Owlcat's history and upcoming projects. Two things really caught my eye: Owlcat's still got hardcore CRPG fans covered, and the studio's bulked up to the heavyweight division. "We will continue to make CRPGs because we love them," Mishulin said of the action-RPG versus CRPG question. "We do not want to become stagnant. We will be trying different approaches for our RPG games, trying to find the best possible fit for the idea of the game. "We want to create the best possible RPGs, we like them, we play them, we get inspired by them and we want our games to feel the same, that we would enjoy them ourselves and hope that they will inspire someone else to create even better ones." Owlcat's first three games share an engine, design sensibility, and overall structure⁠—you're a monarch or otherwise leading a state-level organization⁠—so the very Mass Effect-like The Expanse: Osiris Reborn represents a huge, if exciting, departure . I didn't think there was a danger of the studio permanently pivoting away from the house style that put it on the map, but Mishulin's statement is reassuring. It's also backed up by the other game Owlcat has in development, Warhammer 40K: Dark Heresy. It iterates on Owlcat's CRPG engine and the ruleset of Rogue Trader in a way that echoes the jump from Pathfinder: Kingmaker to Wrath of the Righteous. But it's also a big departure in its own way: Owlcat is trading its customary ruler fantasy and light 4X elements for an ambitious, highly reactive, detective/investigation metagame⁠— it sounds rad . The studio has massively expanded to work on two projects simultaneously: Both PCGamesN and Wccftech have reported that Owlcat currently consists of around 600 employees. Looking at other RPG big boys, Larian was north of 500 at last check-in, and Obsidian is currently in the low 200s following Microsoft's latest layoffs . According to a 2024 fact sheet , CD Projekt Red has 1,134 worldwide employees, while a 2023 financial statement had its heartland studio in Warsaw accounting for 615 of them. BioWare was likely pushing a 500-600 person headcount at its fullest extent in the 2010s (with the Montreal and Austin branches), but back of the napkin math has it now at 100 or fewer employees following post-Veilguard layoffs. It's unclear how many separate offices Owlcat's staff is spread across. Originally founded in Moscow, the developer is currently headquartered in Paphos, Cyprus. This expanded manpower is certainly in the "Yep, that's enough people to handle two RPGs at once" range, and you could imagine Owlcat satisfying both action and CRPG fans by keeping up a multi-game approach, similar to what BioWare managed with Mass Effect and Dragon Age during its golden years.
